title: Handoff, role, or edge?
intro: Three coordination primitives, easily blurred. Which one is each statement describing?

buckets.label: Crew role/task
buckets.hint: Org chart: people and assigned work

cards.text: The emailer takes over the conversation from here — the caller is done
Declared as handoffs=[emailer_agent] with a handoff_description
A 'Senior Financial Researcher' with a goal and a backstory picks up the analysis task
tasks.yaml assigns each piece of work an expected_output and an owner
A hierarchical process gives the team a manager who delegates
A conditional function inspects state and routes to retry or finish
The loop 'act until the evaluator passes' is drawn between named nodes
add_messages merges each node's output into one typed State

debrief: Handoffs move OWNERSHIP of a conversation — delegation between peers, declared per-agent. Crew roles move WORK through an org chart — people-shaped abstraction, YAML-declared, optionally managed. Graph edges move STATE through functions — nothing is delegated, everything is routed, and the routing itself is code you can test. The blur happens because all three end with 'another agent does the next part' — the question to ask is what traveled: the conversation (handoff), the task (role), or the state (edge).
